title: Psalms Chapter 139 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 139 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 139 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 139.

questions.question: Who is the author of the Psalm 139?
questions.explanation: The Psalm is described as a Psalm of David in Psalms 139:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD know about the psalmist according to Psalms 139:1?
questions.explanation: The LORD has searched the psalmist and knows him, which includes knowing his thoughts afar off as stated in Psalms 139:2.

questions.question: According to Psalms 139:3, what is the LORD acquainted with?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD is acquainted with all the psalmist's ways, indicating complete knowledge.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about the knowledge of the LORD in Psalms 139:6?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses that the knowledge of the LORD is too wonderful for him and high, which he cannot attain to.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist believes he can hide from the presence of the LORD.
questions.explanation: The psalmist questions where he could flee from the LORD's presence, indicating he knows he cannot hide (Psalms 139:7).

questions.question: In Psalms 139:8, where does the psalmist say the LORD is present?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that if he ascends into heaven or makes his bed in hell, the LORD is there in both places (Psalms 139:8).

questions.question: What does the psalmist say will lead him in Psalms 139:10?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that even in the uttermost parts of the sea, the hand of the LORD shall lead him (Psalms 139:10).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist believes that darkness can hide him from the LORD.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that darkness does not hide from the LORD and that night is as bright as day (Psalms 139:12).

questions.question: According to Psalms 139:14, how does the psalmist describe his creation?
questions.explanation: The psalmist praises the LORD for making him fearfully and wonderfully, acknowledging the marvelous works of God (Psalms 139:14).

questions.question: What did the LORD see when the psalmist was made in secret according to Psalms 139:15?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that the LORD saw his substance when he was made in secret (Psalms 139:15).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist expresses hate towards those who rise up against the LORD.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that he hates those who hate the LORD and is grieved by those who rise up against Him (Psalms 139:21).

questions.question: In what order does the psalmist ask the LORD to search him and know him?
options: Know my heart, try me, know my thoughts
Try me, know my thoughts, search me
Search me, know my thoughts, know my heart
Know my thoughts, search me, try me
questions.correctAnswer: Search me, know my thoughts, know my heart
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks the LORD to search him first, then know his thoughts, and finally know his heart (Psalms 139:23).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 139 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 139 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:10 say about God's presence?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:10 states, 'Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.' This highlights God's guidance and support regardless of where one is.

questions.question: According to Psalms 139:12, how does God perceive darkness?
options: It is the same as light
questions.correctAnswer: It is the same as light
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:12 explains that 'the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.' This implies that God sees all equally, without distinction.

questions.question: What should a believer conclude about their creation according to Psalms 139:14?
options: They are fearfully and wonderfully made
questions.correctAnswer: They are fearfully and wonderfully made
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:14 states, 'I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works.' This affirms the believer's value and uniqueness in God's creation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:9 suggest about God's omnipresence?
options: He is absent in the sea
He is present in all places
He cannot be found in darkness
questions.correctAnswer: He is present in all places
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:9, the psalmist acknowledges that no matter where he goes, even to the 'uttermost parts of the sea,' God is there, indicating His omnipresence.

questions.question: Does Psalms 139:15 indicate that God is aware of the formation of human life?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:15 states, 'My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret,' confirming that God is fully aware of human life from its very beginning.

questions.question: How does Psalms 139:23 encourage believers in their spiritual journey?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:23, the psalmist asks God to 'Search me, O God, and know my heart,' encouraging believers to be open to God’s scrutiny in their spiritual lives.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 139:17, God's thoughts about us are few and insignificant.
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:17 reveals that 'How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!' indicating that God's thoughts towards us are abundant and valuable, not few.

questions.question: According to Psalms 139:11, what happens when the psalmist is in darkness?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:11 states, 'even the night shall be light about me,' indicating that God's presence makes even darkness light.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 139:24 asks God to lead the believer in the way everlasting.
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:24 concludes with a request for God to 'lead me in the way everlasting,' affirming the believer's desire for divine guidance towards eternal life.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:16 reveal about God's knowledge of us before we were formed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:16 states, 'Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect,' indicating God's intimate knowledge of us even before we were fully formed.

questions.question: How does Psalms 139:19 reflect the psalmist's feelings towards the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:19 expresses the psalmist's strong feelings, stating, 'Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God,' indicating a deep aversion to wickedness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 139:20 indicates that God's enemies speak against Him wickedly.
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:20 notes that 'they speak against thee wickedly,' confirming the reality of opposition faced by God from His enemies.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:3 say about God's acquaintance with us?
options: He is unaware of our thoughts
He is familiar with all our ways
questions.correctAnswer: He is familiar with all our ways
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:3 states, 'Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways,' emphasizing God's comprehensive knowledge of our lives and actions.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 139 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 139.

questions.question: What does the psalmist declare about God's knowledge of him?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses that God knows his thoughts even from afar, as indicated in Psalms 139:2 where it states, 'Thou understandest my thought afar off.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 139, where can one flee from God's presence?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:7-8 emphasizes that there is no escape from God's presence, stating, 'Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?'

questions.question: What is described as 'too wonderful' for the psalmist?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:6, it is written, 'Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it,' referring to God's omniscience.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe the darkness in relation to God?
options: It is a source of fear
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:12 states, 'Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day,' showing that God sees all regardless of light or darkness.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about his creation in his mother's womb?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:13 indicates, 'For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother's womb,' which highlights God's active role in his creation.

questions.question: Which verse talks about God's thoughts being precious?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:17 states, 'How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!' indicating the value of God's thoughts towards the psalmist.

questions.question: What does the psalmist compare God's thoughts to?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:18, the psalmist states, 'If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand,' illustrating the vastness of God's thoughts.

questions.question: In Psalms 139, what does the psalmist express about the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:19 states, 'Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God,' indicating the psalmist's belief in God's judgment against the wicked.

questions.question: What emotion does the psalmist express towards those who hate God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:21 reveals, 'Do not I hate them, O LORD, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?' showing his deep emotional response.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist claims to hate the wicked with a 'perfect hatred.'
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:22 states, 'I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies,' which confirms the psalmist's strong feelings against the wicked.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request God to do in Psalms 139:23?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:23, the psalmist asks, 'Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts,' seeking divine insight into his inner self.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist believes that God can lead him in the way everlasting.
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:24 concludes with 'and lead me in the way everlasting,' indicating the psalmist's faith in God's guidance.

questions.question: Which other book of the Bible emphasizes God's omnipresence similar to Psalms 139?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:1 echoes the theme of God's omnipresence, stating, 'The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool,' similar to Psalms 139:7-8.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the idea of being 'fearfully and wonderfully made'?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:10 states, 'For we are his workmanship,' reflecting the same sentiment as Psalms 139:14 about being wonderfully made.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'thoughts' (מַחֲשָׁבוֹת) imply in Psalms 139:17?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'thoughts' in Psalms 139:17 suggests 'plans' or 'intentions,' emphasizing God's active and purposeful thoughts towards us.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 139 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 139 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:1 reveal about God's relationship with humanity?
options: God is only aware of our actions
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:1 states, 'O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me,' indicating an intimate and comprehensive knowledge of humanity by God.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated in Psalms 139:5?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:5, 'Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me,' it shows God's complete knowledge and awareness of our lives, highlighting His omniscience.

questions.question: How does Psalms 139:14 contribute to our understanding of human creation?
options: Humans are created fearfully and wonderfully
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are created fearfully and wonderfully
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:14 states, 'I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made,' emphasizing the intentional and marvelous nature of human creation.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can we gain from combining Psalms 139:13 and 139:16?
options: God's knowledge of individuals begins at birth
God's knowledge of us precedes our physical formation
God does not care about our creation
questions.correctAnswer: God's knowledge of us precedes our physical formation
questions.explanation: Verses 139:13 and 139:16 together show that God possesses knowledge of us even in our unformed state, indicating His sovereignty over our creation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:8 teach about God's presence?
options: God is only present in heaven
God's presence is limited to the righteous
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:8, 'If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there,' it affirms God's omnipresence.

questions.question: Which part of God's character is highlighted in Psalms 139:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:17, 'How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!' illustrates God's thoughtful consideration towards humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 139:24 urge the believer to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:24, 'And see if there be any wicked way in me,' calls for self-examination and repentance, emphasizing the need for internal purity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 139:11 address the concept of darkness?
options: Darkness is the absence of God
questions.explanation: In Psalms 139:11, 'Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me,' it affirms that darkness does not hinder God's presence or knowledge.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'my substance was not hid from thee' in Psalms 139:15 imply?
options: God is unaware of our being
God knows everything about our creation
God does not care about our existence
questions.correctAnswer: God knows everything about our creation
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:15 highlights God's intimate knowledge of our being even before we were born, showing His sovereignty over all creation.

questions.question: What insight about human thoughts can be drawn from Psalms 139:2?
options: God is unaware of our thoughts
God understands our thoughts from afar
Human thoughts are irrelevant to God
questions.correctAnswer: God understands our thoughts from afar
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:2 states, 'Thou understandest my thought afar off,' indicating God's deep understanding of our inner thoughts, regardless of distance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 139:19-20, what is the psalmist's attitude towards the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:21-22 expresses a strong aversion to those who oppose God, indicating the psalmist's perfect hatred toward the wicked.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to do in Psalms 139:23?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:23, 'Search me, O God, and know my heart,' indicates a desire for God to examine his inner self, seeking purity and righteousness.

questions.question: What aspect of God's character is evident in Psalms 139:12?
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:12 states, 'the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day,' showcasing God's omnipresence where darkness cannot conceal anything from Him.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 139:10 and 139:8 convey about God's guidance?
options: God's guidance is only in good times
God's guidance is absent in suffering
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:10 and 139:8 together reveal that God's hand leads us regardless of our circumstances, affirming His constant guidance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is not involved in human creation. What does Psalms 139:13-16 actually teach?
options: God knows us before we are formed
God has no role in creation
God only cares about perfect beings
questions.correctAnswer: God knows us before we are formed
questions.explanation: Psalms 139:13-16 teaches that God is intimately involved in our creation, knowing us even in our mother’s womb, countering the sceptics' claim.
